name: Environmentalism
summary: Environmentalism seeks to protect natural systems and to make human use of them sustainable. Its defining texts hold that nature has a standing beyond its usefulness (Leopold), that present generations must not compromise those who come after (the Brundtland report) and that the poor and developing countries need priority and fairer international economics. Beyond ecology it has little doctrine, and its strands divide on growth, nuclear power, technology and ownership, so most social and economic questions are left unanswered.
scope: The mainstream modern environmental movement and its political expression in green politics, drawing on Leopold's land ethic, the Brundtland report, Carson-era conservation and the SEP's account of environmental ethics. It excludes free-market environmentalism and eco-fascism as minority or fringe strands, and answers dark-green and bright-green splits as 0 or low where adherents divide.
